➡️ Hong Kong man loses HK$13 million in fake crypto investment app scam 

🌐 A Hong Kong man in his 70s has lost more than HK$13 million ($1.67 million) after a self-described cryptocurrency investment expert contacted him through WhatsApp and directed him to a fake trading app. The latest case began when the elderly man received an unsolicited WhatsApp message from someone claiming to be a cryptocurrency investment expert from Singapore. The person introduced him to what was presented as a crypto platform offering favorable exchange rates, low fees and withdrawals at any time.

‼️ Following the instructions he received, the man opened a cryptocurrency wallet and purchased Tether (USDT) and Ethereum (ETH). He was then told to download an investment application supplied by the scammer and transfer the cryptocurrency to designated wallet addresses as investment capital.

📣 Seeing his account balance rise inside the app, the victim became less suspicious and continued sending more cryptocurrency to the wallets provided by the scammer. The fraud only became clear when he tried to withdraw his funds and was repeatedly prevented from doing so under different pretexts. By the time the victim realized the investment platform was fraudulent, his losses had exceeded HK$13 million.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

As we predicted, the hype around TON DNS has begun. The hype began with Four-Digit domains (hereinafter referred to as 4N domains). People are "burning" their 100 TON on the TON DNS smart contract and transferring this value to NFTs (similar to Banksy's work). 

On February 13, the last domain from the Club 100 (0074.ton), was minted, on February 17, the thousandth domain (5755.ton), and on February 28, the last domain from the 1k Club (0863.ton).

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

8. Repeating the success of ENS, this time in the form of a utility — a shell in Telegram (because TON DNS renewal costs pennies, compared to $160 per year for a 4-digit ENS).

🌍 Iran parliament commission approves penalties for violators of Hormuz laws

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Commission has approved new penalties for vessels violating transit regulations in the Strait of Hormuz as part of legislative steps to consolidate Iran's sovereign control over the world’s most critical energy chokepoint.

Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesperson for the commission, said on Tuesday that the commission has reviewed and approved Articles 13, 14, and 15 of the “Strategic Action to Ensure Security and Development of the Strait of Hormuz” bill.
​
The bill formalizes the rules of engagement and transit within the vital waterway, backing Iran’s military dominance with severe legal and economic deterrents, he said, adding that, under the newly approved Article 13, any vessel failing to comply with Iranian transit regulations will face immediate and heavy consequences.
​
In addition to the penalties outlined in Article 5 of the Islamic Penal Code, authorities now have permission to confiscate 20 percent of the violating vessel’s cargo or extract its equivalent financial value, said the spokesman.
​
Furthermore, the offending ship will be temporarily impounded by Iranian maritime forces until penalties and fines are fully paid, noted Ghashghavi.
​
To ensure the precise and professional enforcement of these regulations, the Judiciary has been mandated to establish specialized court branches, he said.
​
These tribunals will be staffed by judges and experts specializing in maritime law and the international law of the sea, ensuring that Iran’s legal framework aligns with its strategic enforcement capabilities, explained the lawmaker.
​
Article 14, he maintained, establishes strict domestic accountability, stipulating that any individual or legal entity whose actions or negligence lead to the failure, delay, or incomplete implementation of the law will face Grade 5 punishments under Article 19 of the Islamic Penal Code.
​
Crucially, a supplementary note to Article 14 asserts Iran’s absolute legal sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, added the Parliamentarian.
​
It dictates that any future bilateral or multilateral international agreements or binding documents regarding the Strait of Hormuz must strictly comply with Articles 77, 125, 176, and 57 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran. This effectively nullifies any external attempts to impose foreign navigation frameworks on the Strait without Tehran’s explicit constitutional consent, he said.
​
To maintain rigorous oversight of the waterway, Article 15 holds that the General Staff of the Armed Forces are to oversee the law’s execution, Ghashghavi said, adding that the military high command is required to submit comprehensive implementation reports to the National Security Commission every three months, either directly or through the Ministry of Defense.
​
For the bill to become law, the commission must finalize it, after which it must be sent to the full floor of Parliament for a final vote by all lawmakers, pending approval by the Constitutional Council.
​
The advancement of this bill comes as Iran continues to consolidate its unprecedented control over the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the illegal US-Israeli war of aggression in late February 2026.

🔘 StablecoinX, backed by Pantera and other major funds, acquired nearly 20% of ENA. The project is behind the digital dollar USDe.

🔘 SDC has accumulated around 10% of SKY. The project is building a lending and digital-dollar system without a traditional bank.

🔘 Hyperliquid Strategies acquired roughly $2.2 billion worth of HYPE – the token of one of the largest decentralized crypto exchanges. The company now controls around 12.5% of all HYPE.

There are plenty of other examples like these. But all of these purchases point to the same broader trend: money is flowing into lending, exchanges, digital dollars, and payment infrastructure.
